Low actuation force is not low released energy
A rolling retainer can turn high axial retention into a small trigger action by changing the contact geometry. Its springs, rotor and bolt still contain and exchange energy. A compact resettable mechanism is therefore a serious alternative to punching every healthy interface, while its current profile, stroke, binding, transverse loading, recapture, life and inspection remain essential new operations.

A useful candidate is a retained metering path that takes the boundary reaction, controls its reduction and remains engaged until the last loaded contact is actually free. Only then may a reusable retainer open or a rare-fault escape cut. A complete capture cage retains the internal jam throughout. This is a physical organization to construct, not an available6D force actuator or an instruction to overwrite reaction with zero. Every temporary metering contact must itself be retrieved.
